title: Best Trade Show Booth Designers (2026): Booths That Draw Visitors
description: How to hire a trade show booth designer: graphics, layout, print files, how to brief it, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: Trade booth designers create the graphics and layout for exhibition stands: back walls, banners, counters, pop-up displays and sometimes 3D booth plans. A good booth tells visitors who you are from across the hall and invites them in. Projects go wrong when the design ignores the booth supplier's templates, text is too small to read from a distance, or files are not ready for large-format printing. This guide helps you get a booth that works on the show floor.

faq.q: Do I need a 3D design or just graphics?
faq.a: If you rent a standard booth, print graphics for its panels may be enough. Custom booths benefit from a 3D layout that shows walls, counters and lighting.

faq.q: What files does the printer need?
faq.a: Usually high-resolution PDFs at full size with bleed, in the color mode the printer requests. Get the printer's template first.

faq.q: How much text should be on the booth?
faq.a: Very little. Visitors scan booths quickly. A clear brand, a short message and one strong image work best.
Ask for editable files and a modular design, so panels can be updated or rearranged for future shows.
Large-format printing and shipping can take weeks. Plan the design deadline around the printer's schedule.
